sections.heading: FOCIL Devnet 0 Client Readiness
sections.summary: Most CL/EL client pairs have devnet-0 branches ready; local interop will be attempted before launching devnet 0.
sections.body:
- **ethrex (EL):** Updated implementation to latest spec tests; passing all tests but some fixtures/harness issues found. PRs opened against execution-specs repo with local fixes.
- **Teku (CL):** Devnet-0 branch ready, includes recent spec changes (signed inclusion list max size, transaction emptiness check). Local Kurtosis interop run successfully with Lodestar, ethrex, and Besu. Docker image published. Minor timing issues still being investigated.
- **Besu (EL):** Devnet-0 branch should be ready; passing all EIP tests. Still needs to verify whether Barnabas's spec change affects EL.
  - Jihoon clarified that regardless of gossip rule decisions, EL should not be affected.
- **Reth (EL):** Non-stale branch `reth-fossil-devnet-0` created by Matt; basic interop with other clients and Hive tests run. Not 100% but mostly ready. Reth team is aware of the effort.
- **Nethermind (EL):** Mark reported that Nethermind merged FOCIL on the `focil-devnet-0` branch, passing all tests, but has not yet tried interop with other clients.
- **Lighthouse (CL):** FOCIL devnet-0 branch updated from alpha 13 to alpha 14 (Barnabas opened the PR). Simple Kurtosis runs with Teku found no problems.
- **Lodestar (CL):** Still in development; PRs for inclusion list committee derivation and signature verification are in review.
- Jihoon confirmed a 2×2 (two CL + two EL) client combination is sufficient to launch devnet 0. Will attempt local interop and launch if successful.
- Nico Flaig asked whether anyone has tested unhappy cases yet; no one has. Jihoon suggested focusing on happy paths for initial devnets and testing unhappy cases in subsequent ones.

sections.heading: Spec PR 5576: Inclusion List Size Limit and Gossip Rules
sections.summary: Agreement to set ~40 KB gossip size limit, reject empty transactions in ILs, and ignore empty inclusion lists.
sections.body:
- [PR 5544](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5544) (IL forkchoice key changed to slot-independent root) was merged and included in alpha 14.
- [PR 5576](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5576) proposes a ~40 KB pub-sub/peer limit for inclusion list messages on the CL gossip layer.
  - The 40 KB figure derives from assuming minimum 1-byte transactions: 8192 × 1-byte txs + 8192 × 4-byte SSZ offsets = 41,112 bytes.
  - Justin Traglia provided the calculation in chat; with 128 txs it would be 8192 + 128 × 4 = 8,704 bytes.
  - Previous spec assumed only one transaction per IL — an oversight since the max individual transaction size (8 KB) was used as the list size limit.
  - No objections to the 40 KB limit.
- **Empty transaction check:** PR proposes rejecting ILs containing zero-length transactions as a gossip rule.
  - Justin Traglia and Mehdi Aouadi supported it as a defensive mechanism, noting transactions are opaque to the CL.
  - Fabio Di Fabio confirmed a zero-byte transaction makes no sense and the check is safe; referenced [engine_newPayloadV1 spec](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/paris.md#engine_newpayloadv1) which already requires non-zero-length transactions.
  - Agreement: add the empty-transaction rejection rule.
- **Empty inclusion list check:** Separate question on whether to filter out ILs with an empty transaction list (i.e., no transactions at all).
  - Justin Traglia initially leaned toward treating empty ILs as valid ("they just don't have any opinions") but ultimately leaned toward adding an ignore rule.
  - soispoke noted it is limited spam (max 16 includers per slot, must be a committee member) and not a major DoS risk, but still unnecessary bandwidth.
  - Agreement: empty inclusion lists should be ignored (not rejected) at the gossip layer, distinct from the reject action for malformed ILs containing empty transactions.

sections.heading: Engine API Specification for getInclusionList
sections.summary: Jihoon will open a PR to specify that getInclusionList must return non-empty, valid transactions, mirroring newPayloadV1 language.
sections.body:
- Fabio suggested adding explicit language to the Engine API spec for `getInclusionList` requiring transactions to be at least 1 byte, consistent with `engine_newPayloadV1`.
- Justin Florentine (Besu) supported over-specifying given known JSON RPC divergence issues across clients.
- Justin Traglia agreed: "when in doubt, be explicit."
- Jihoon will open a PR to add this specification.

sections.heading: Hive Testing for Inclusion List Construction
sections.summary: Hive testing of IL construction is complicated by non-deterministic censorship detection; discussion deferred to ACD and further async work.
sections.body:
- Fabio reported Besu had a bug in `getInclusionList` that Mehdi discovered but EF tests did not catch, advocating for Hive test coverage.
- Jihoon noted `getInclusionList` output is non-deterministic — a client can legitimately return any subset of mempool transactions (including an empty IL), making deterministic test expectations difficult.
- Justin Florentine proposed a debug/test namespace API where a Hive test could explicitly add transactions to the mempool and instruct the client to censor them, enabling deterministic testing.
  - Fabio expressed concern that a debug endpoint might not exercise production code paths.
  - Jihoon noted such tests could still be flaky (passing even when bugs exist).
- Justin Florentine raised a broader question: how committed is the community to having clients implement different censorship-detection heuristics?
  - soispoke argued there is no objective censorship detection function — it is always heuristic-based. Different client heuristics make gaming harder, though future coordination toward shared rules is possible.
  - Nico Flaig noted the existing `shouldOverrideBuilder` flag has been in the spec for ~3 years but only Nethermind implemented it, and it never fired on mainnet. Referenced [execution-APIs PR #425](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/425).
- Jihoon will discuss the Hive testing question with the testing team (Steele) and bring it to the next ACD call for wider input.

sections.heading: Incentive Design Considerations for Includers
sections.summary: Future rewards/penalties for includers were discussed briefly; no concrete changes proposed, but designing with extensibility in mind was encouraged.
sections.body:
- soispoke suggested designing FOCIL gossip validity rules as if rewards or penalties for includers might be added later, to make the infrastructure extensible.
- Justin Florentine expressed skepticism about being able to anticipate the right design choices for incentives, given the non-deterministic nature of the mempool and the difficulty of proving negatives.
- Justin Traglia noted includer rewards are unlikely in the foreseeable future and the empty-IL ignore rule could simply be removed later if needed.
- No changes to current design were proposed based on this discussion.

sections.heading: EIP-8369: FOCIL and Frames Interaction
sections.summary: EIP-8369 on FOCIL-frames interaction flagged for review; ethrex is prototyping; deeper discussion planned for the next FOCIL breakout.
sections.body:
- soispoke flagged [EIP-8369](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12110), an EIP focused on understanding how FOCIL and frame transactions interact, requesting review from FOCIL experts.
- With frame transactions expected to be SFI'd, the interaction between frame transactions and FOCIL needs to be resolved.
- ethrex is actively prototyping and backing this effort.
- soispoke explained the related concept of VOPS (Validity-Only Partial State) — the subset of state mempool nodes must retain to evaluate transaction validity, which becomes significantly more complex with frame transactions.
- Jihoon proposed using the next FOCIL breakout (in two weeks) for a deeper discussion and Q&A on EIP-8369 with soispoke.
